findings.title: Saving the address fails and clears what the user typed
findings.expected: Within 10 s the user sees an error message (role=alert or error wording) instead of a spinner running past 30 s; no blank or crashed screen; data is never shown as empty because of the failure; the typed input is kept; the action is never shown as done; after the fault is removed the step completes without a full reload.
findings.actual: The 11-character address was cleared (length 11 to 0) and no message appeared within 10 s; saving again saved an empty address.
findings.user_impact: The user retypes the address without knowing why it vanished, or saves a blank one.
findings.fix: In address() (app.js), drop form.reset() from the catch block; keep the input and show an error with a retry button.
findings.verification_step: Rerun scenarios S08, S09 with run_resilience.py --runs 2: no lost_input effect.

findings.title: A failed address save shows no message
findings.expected: Within 10 s the user sees an error message (role=alert or error wording) instead of a spinner running past 30 s; no blank or crashed screen; data is never shown as empty because of the failure; the typed input is kept; the action is never shown as done; after the fault is removed the step completes without a full reload.
findings.actual: After the 500 or going offline, nothing appeared: no error element and no error wording within 10 s.
findings.user_impact: The user believes the address was saved, or doesn't know it wasn't.
findings.fix: Show an error (role=alert) in the catch block of address(), with a Try again button.
findings.verification_step: Rerun scenarios S08, S09 with run_resilience.py --runs 2: no silent_failure effect.

findings.title: A hung status request leaves the tracking page spinning forever
findings.expected: Within 10 s the user sees an error message (role=alert or error wording) instead of a spinner running past 30 s; no blank or crashed screen; data is never shown as empty because of the failure; after the fault is removed the step completes without a full reload.
findings.actual: With /api/status/* hanging, the spinner was still showing after 30 s, with no error.
findings.user_impact: The user waits indefinitely for the parcel status.
findings.fix: Give the status fetch a timeout (AbortController, about 10 s) and show an error with a retry button when it fires.
findings.verification_step: Rerun scenarios S01 with run_resilience.py --runs 2: no endless_loading effect.

findings.title: A failed status request shows a broken status as if it were real
findings.expected: Within 10 s the user sees an error message (role=alert or error wording) instead of a spinner running past 30 s; no blank or crashed screen; data is never shown as empty because of the failure; after the fault is removed the step completes without a full reload.
findings.actual: With a 500 on /api/status/*, the page showed "undefined: undefined" and "Last scan: none yet", where the baseline showed "Sorting centre", and no error.
findings.user_impact: The user reads that the parcel has not been scanned.

findings.verification_step: Rerun scenarios S04, S05 with run_resilience.py --runs 2: no misleading_state effect.

findings.title: The orders screen can't be retried without reloading
findings.expected: Within 10 s the user sees an error message (role=alert or error wording) instead of a spinner running past 30 s; no blank or crashed screen; data is never shown as empty because of the failure; after the fault is removed the step completes without a full reload.
findings.actual: After the fault was removed, there was no retry control, and choosing "My parcels" again (the same #orders route) does nothing, so the screen stays wrong until a full reload.
findings.user_impact: The user is stuck on an error or empty screen until they reload.
findings.fix: Add a retry control to the orders screen's error and empty states, and re-render on a click of the current route.
findings.verification_step: Rerun scenarios S04, S05, S06 with run_resilience.py --runs 2: no no_recovery effect.

findings.title: A failed recommendations widget takes down the whole orders screen
findings.expected: Within 10 s the user sees an error message (role=alert or error wording) instead of a spinner running past 30 s; no blank or crashed screen; data is never shown as empty because of the failure; after the fault is removed the step completes without a full reload.
findings.actual: With /api/recommendations returning 500, rendering threw (recs.items is undefined) and the route boundary replaced the screen with "Something went wrong" (B2).
findings.user_impact: An optional widget hides the user's parcels.
findings.fix: Load recommendations separately and render the orders without them when they fail (check recs.items, or a boundary around the widget only).
findings.verification_step: Rerun scenarios S06 with run_resilience.py --runs 2: no crash_b2 effect.

findings.title: A failed help chunk leaves a blank screen
findings.expected: The screen keeps its content or shows an error within 10 s; no blank screen.
findings.actual: With chunk-help.js failing to load, the app root was emptied and nothing was shown.
findings.user_impact: The user sees an empty page with only the header.
findings.fix: In help(), show an error with a retry that re-requests the chunk, instead of clearing the screen.
findings.verification_step: Rerun scenarios S11 with run_resilience.py --runs 2: no chunk_failure effect.

findings.title: The notices poll retries a 503 every 200 ms and ignores Retry-After
findings.expected: Within 10 s the user sees an error message (role=alert or error wording) instead of a spinner running past 30 s; no blank or crashed screen; data is never shown as empty because of the failure; no more than 10 requests in 30 s and none before Retry-After; after the fault is removed the step completes without a full reload.
findings.actual: With /api/notices returning 503 and Retry-After: 5, the client sent 52 requests to the same URL within 10706 ms (gaps about 205 ms), each sooner than Retry-After.
findings.user_impact: Every open tab hammers a struggling service, making the outage worse.
findings.fix: In notices(), honour Retry-After and back off exponentially with jitter (for example 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, capped).
findings.verification_step: Rerun scenarios S07 with run_resilience.py --runs 2: no retry_storm effect.

headline.summary: 13 scenarios planned in 5 flows; 11 ran twice each after clean baselines, with 8 fault types injected in the browser. The returns flow is broken without any fault: its baseline never showed the returns form (the app has no #returns route), so its scenario is untested. One scenario never triggered its fault (S12: the orders were already loaded), so it tested nothing. 9 findings, all reproduced: the address save loses input silently, the tracking page can spin forever, failures are shown as empty data, and a failed optional widget or chunk takes out the screen. The optimistic "Mark as received" rolled back with a message, and the missing font only logs an error.

Not reachable from the browser (track / open tracking): the courier scan feed behind /api/status: the API builds the status on the server; a failure between the API and its own data sources happens server-side, where a browser-side fault cannot reach (only the /api/status response that carries the result).
Browser-side faults only; server-side faults (between the backend and its data sources) were not tried.
One desktop Chromium profile; mobile profiles, Firefox and WebKit were not run.
Not tried: 401/403 mid-flow, 429, 5 MB and HTML payloads, flapping endpoints and service workers; see the coverage table for what ran.
Recovery was tried without a reload, through the app's retry control or the step's actions; a reload was not counted as recovery.
